title: Culinary Concept Development Kitchen

stages.name: interpretBrief
stages.algorithm: Translate the culinary brief into desired experience, service style, supplied dietary requirements, equipment, and budget constraints. Distinguish preferences from mandatory restrictions and use only verified ingredient and allergen information rather than inferring safety from a dish name.
stages.gate: Mandatory dietary and operational constraints are explicit and source-backed.

stages.name: generateDishes
stages.algorithm: Invent distinct dishes using available ingredients and approved culinary procedures, explaining flavor, texture, and service intent. Propose substitutions only when their properties and dietary implications are verified, and preserve specialist food-safety review where needed.
stages.gate: Concepts respect verified restrictions and documented kitchen capability.

stages.name: constructMenu
stages.algorithm: Assemble a balanced menu whose dishes work together across preparation effort, equipment, pacing, and customer choice. Identify shared components and bottlenecks, preserve meaningful alternatives for required diets, and avoid creating variety only through superficial garnish changes.
stages.gate: Menu-level feasibility and required dietary coverage pass.

stages.name: planAndCost
stages.algorithm: Use exact recipe scaling, inventory, costing, and scheduling services to build preparation and service plans. Account for yield, waste, shared equipment, and approved handling requirements; preserve traceability from purchased ingredients to served dishes.
stages.gate: Exact quantities, costs, equipment capacity, and approved handling constraints reconcile.

stages.name: reviewTastings
stages.algorithm: Interpret structured tasting and service rehearsal notes to identify creative and practical improvements. Distinguish subjective preference from repeatable defects, revise the smallest relevant components, and revalidate cost, dietary information, and service dependencies after every change.
stages.gate: Revised menu passes hard checks; culinary quality remains chef-reviewed rather than self-certified.

operational_details: A supplier substitutes an ingredient: recheck verified allergen and dietary data before use.
Yield differs from the estimate: update exact batch quantities and cost.
Two dishes need the same equipment simultaneously: replan service rather than assuming unlimited capacity.
A tasting change affects a shared sauce: propagate it to every dish and disclosure.
A menu label claims allergen-free preparation: require the venue’s verified controls and qualified approval.

scenario.representative_episode: A seasonal menu must use surplus ingredients, provide several dietary options, and fit a small kitchen with one shared cooking bottleneck.
scenario.independent_truth: Fictional ingredient properties, verified dietary records, exact recipe and resource calculations, and chef-led tasting preferences.
